        """Test that reindex works correctly with iterator targets."""
        # This tests the change in the reindex method where ensure_has_len was replaced

        from pandas import Index
        
        # Create an index
        idx = Index(['a', 'b', 'c'])

        """Test the old behavior - single space trimming."""
        # This should work the same way as before
        strings = [" a", " b", " c"]
        result = trim_front(strings)
        expected = ["a", "b", "c"]
        assert result == expected

        """Test the new behavior - trim minimum leading spaces."""

import pytest

    def test_reindex_with_iterator_target(self):
        """Test that reindex works correctly with iterator targets.
        
        This tests the specific change where ensure_has_len(target) was replaced
        with is_iterator(target) check and direct list conversion.
        """
        from pandas import Index
        
        # Create an index
        idx = Index(['a', 'b', 'c'])

        # because ensure_has_len would convert it to list, but the old way was less
        # robust in some edge cases
        target_gen = (x for x in ['b', 'a'])
        
        # This should work without error - the old code would have converted
        # the iterator to a list using ensure_has_len, but now it should do so
        # using is_iterator check
        result = idx.reindex(target_gen)
        
        # Verify the result
        expected_index = Index(['b', 'a'])
        expected_values = [1, 0]
        
        assert result[0].equals(expected_index)
        assert list(result[1]) == expected_values

        expected = ["  a", " b", "c"]  # Trim 1 space from each
        assert result == expected

        """Test strings with no leading spaces."""
        strings = ["a", "b", "c"]
        result = trim_front(strings)
        expected = ["a", "b", "c"]
        assert result == expected

        """Test empty list."""
        strings = []

        expected = []

    """Test reindex with iterator targets - demonstrates the is_iterator change.
    
    This test verifies that the reindex method correctly handles iterator targets
    by using the more explicit is_iterator check instead of the generic ensure_has_len.
    """
    from pandas import Index
    
    # Create test index
    idx = Index(['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f'])
    
    # Test with iterator (generator) - this exercises the is_iterator logic
    target_gen = (x for x in ['f', 'c', 'a', 'e'])
    
    # This should work correctly with the new implementation
    result = idx.reindex(target_gen)
    
    # Verify correct behavior
    expected_index = Index(['f', 'c', 'a', 'e'])
    expected_values = [5, 2, 0, 4]
    
    assert result[0].equals(expected_index)
    assert list(result[1]) == expected_values


def test_trim_front_algorithm_improvement():
    """Test the improved trim_front algorithm - minimum leading spaces approach.
    
    The trim_front function was changed from a loop-based approach to a 
    minimum-leading-spaces approach for better efficiency and clearer logic.
    
    Old approach: while all strings start with space, remove one space from each (n iterations)
    New approach: calculate minimum leading spaces, remove that many from all (1 iteration)
    """
    from pandas.core.indexes.base import trim_front
    
    # Test basic functionality
    assert trim_front([" a", " b", " c"]) == ["a", "b", "c"]
    
    # Test with multiple leading spaces - the new algorithm trims minimum from all
    assert trim_front(["   a", "  b", " c"]) == ["  a", " b", "c"]
    
    # Test mixed cases
    assert trim_front(["  a", "   b", " c", "    d"]) == [" a", "  b", "c", "   d"]
    
    # Test edge cases that show the algorithm works correctly
    assert trim_front([]) == []
    assert trim_front(["a", "b", "c"]) == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert trim_front(["   ", "  ", " "]) == ["  ", " ", ""]


def test_trim_front_comprehensive_edge_cases():
    """Comprehensive edge case testing for trim_front function."""
    from pandas.core.indexes.base import trim_front
    
    # Test with empty strings mixed in
    result = trim_front(["  a", "", " b"])
    # Should not trim empty string (0 leading spaces) but trim others
    assert result == ["  a", "", " b"]
    
    # Test with strings that have no leading spaces
    result = trim_front(["a", "b", "c"])
    assert result == ["a", "b", "c"]
    
    # Test with all spaces
    result = trim_front(["   ", "  ", " "])
    assert result == ["  ", " ", ""]
    
    # Test with single character strings
    result = trim_front([" a", "b", " c"])
    assert result == ["a", "b", "c"]
